title: The ind-etale subsite is a basis
statement:
Every pro-etale object over an affine $X$ has a cover by objects of $\mathcal
B_X$. Every covering of a basis object has a refinement by a finite covering
of basis objects. Fibre products of basis objects over a basis object remain
in the basis. Restriction to this basis determines a sheaf and its morphisms
uniquely and detects isomorphisms of sheaves.

proof.text: Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of a pro-etale object $U$, the restriction to this open is flat because its stalk maps are unchanged. Its diagonal is the pullback of the flat diagonal of $U/X$ along the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B\to U\times_XU$; this pullback is the diagonal of the restriction, and on affines its coordinate ring is $B\otimes_A B$. Its stalk maps are unchanged too. The affine flatness criterion, applied to this morphism and its diagonal, shows that $A\to B$ is weakly etale in the ring sense. Apply the named weak-etale refinement construction and its theorem to obtain faithfully flat ind-etale $B\to B'$ with $A\to B'$ ind-etale. Its spectrum is surjective by the faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum lemma and is weakly etale by ind-etale stability. It is affine, so the inverse image of any affine open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine. If $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine and $p\in V$, the spectrum-surjectivity lemma gives a prime $q\subset B'$ contracting to $p$; since $p$ lies in $V$, $q$ lies in the inverse image of $V$. Thus that inverse image surjects onto $V$, and this singleton is a covering by the stated covering definition. It is a basis object. Over all affine opens this covers the original object: for any affine open $W\subset U$, choose finitely many principal opens of $W$ lying in affine opens of $U$. Their inverse images under the corresponding affine refinements are affine opens, and their images cover $W$. For a covering of a basis object $V=\operatorname{Spec}D$, the pro-etale covering definition selects finitely many affine opens in the members whose images cover $V$. Refine each selected affine piece over $D$ by the same construction. The faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum lemma shows that the refinements still cover these pieces. Their maps to the affine $V$ are affine and weakly etale; inverse images of any affine open of $V$ are therefore affine and have images covering that open. Thus this finite family is a covering of $V$; composition with $A\to D$ makes every refinement a basis object. For fibre products of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $\operatorname{Spec}D$ in the basis, the relative-map clause of ind-etale stability makes $D\to B$ and $D\to C$ ind-etale. Base change and composition make $D\to B\otimes_D C$ ind-etale, and then $A\to B\otimes_D C$ ind-etale. The affine spectrum of this tensor product is the required basis fibre product.

Take the small skeleton and universes of the pro-etale-site definition, and its full subcategory of basis objects. The inclusion $u:\mathcal B_X\to X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is fully faithful because every morphism between basis objects is retained by the full-subcategory definition. In particular it is locally full: any morphism between its images lifts already on the identity cover; it is locally faithful: equality of images is equality before restriction, again on the identity cover. Step 1 gives cover-density. A sieve on a basis object is covering for the induced topology exactly when its image generates a covering sieve in the full site. This is the topology of the basis definition: any such full-site covering has a finite basis refinement by step 1, and each basis covering is a full-site covering. Apply the existing dense-subsite comparison theorem to this fully faithful inclusion and these topologies. For set-valued sheaves all required small structured-arrow limits exist: they are subsets of products consisting of compatible families. The same construction with coordinatewise operations gives the required limits for abelian groups and modules over a fixed commutative ring. The cited theorem therefore says specifically that restriction along $u$ is an equivalence, not merely that some equivalence exists.

An inverse to the restriction equivalence in step 2 extends a basis sheaf, uniquely up to the unique isomorphism compatible with its specified restriction. Full faithfulness identifies the sets of sheaf morphisms with the morphisms of their restrictions. If a sheaf morphism restricts to an isomorphism, lift its inverse by fullness; the two inverse identities lift by faithfulness. Thus restriction determines sheaves and their morphisms in the usual categorical sense and detects isomorphisms.

lean.note: The listed existing declarations collectively state all clauses: cover-density of the full inclusion, finite jointly surjective families inside any covering sieve, scheme-computed pullbacks in AffineProEt, and equivalence by the actual restriction functor. Apply them to affine S, when AffineProEt is precisely the ind-etale affine basis of the dependency record. Jointly surjective finite families of affine basis objects are pro-etale coverings; membership in the sieve generated by the original cover gives refinement. The equivalence determines objects up to the unique isomorphism compatible with restriction, identifies morphisms and reflects isomorphisms. No module or statement correction.
